- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive and recent highs are followed by a spike; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% after a strong upward sentiment surge.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or shows recent decline; add 3–7% to forecast if sentiment dips below 0.30 or shows sustained negativity.
- Avoid over-optimistic 30-day forecasts when recent 7–14 day mean is below 70; adjust downward by 2–5% if sentiment is weak or volatile.
- Correct for lagged mean reversion: if forecast is 3–5% above recent 14-day average, reduce by 1–3% if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- Suppress overshoot after sharp spikes: if forecast exceeds true outcome by >10% in first 5 days post-spike, reduce by 10–15% to avoid overcorrection.
- Use sentiment as a volatility filter: if sentiment > 0.70, reduce forecast variance by 10–15%; if sentiment < 0.30, increase variance by 5–10% to reflect risk.
